title: Reset tests insert the same unique active grant twice
scenario: Run both reset methods in one Spring context, in either order. Both authenticate the persistent otp-admin account and grant security.mfa_reset.
expected: Each method reaches its reset/security assertions independently of execution order.
actual: The second method inserts an already-existing active grant and violates user_grant_active_uk before testing the endpoint.
evidence: Static source evidence at lines 81–82,108,141–143; no grant cleanup at AfterEach lines 44–47. V4__grants_and_audit.sql:22 defines UNIQUE(user_id, permission) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL. Container execution NOT_RUN; this is an identified fixture defect, not an observed CI failure.
suggested_fix: Use separate synthetic administrators per method or explicitly restore grants; do not rely on method order.
repro_test: Run MfaResetIntegrationTest with both test methods against PostgreSQL/Keycloak; verify the second grant insertion succeeds after fixture isolation.

title: Default-policy test overwrites the migration defaults it claims to verify
scenario: V31 accidentally seeds STAFF or KITCHEN as REQUIRED or DISABLED; run the preview-default test.
expected: The new test detects a non-OPTIONAL initial value for every category.
actual: BeforeEach calls resetPolicies(), which rewrites every row to OPTIONAL, so assertions at lines 100–101 cannot detect the seed regression. Resolver and UI fixtures also hardcode OPTIONAL. The real-token test only probes a customer.
evidence: Static fixture/control-flow evidence: MfaPolicyIntegrationTest.java:49–60,98–107; V31__mfa_policy.sql:14 is the production seed. Container execution NOT_RUN.
suggested_fix: Assert all three defaults in a fresh migrated database before mutating any policy; keep policy-reset fixtures separate from migration-default verification.
repro_test: Mutation check: change only STAFF seed to REQUIRED in a disposable test checkout; the default test should fail without a setup rewrite.

title: Session termination assertion checks a response flag rather than invalidation
scenario: Provider logout stops terminating sessions but reset still removes a factor and returns sessionsEnded=true; or preference disable skips provider logout.
expected: An existing refresh token or SSO session cannot continue after reset/disable, subject to the documented access-token expiry window.
actual: Reset test checks only sessionsEnded=true and then opens a new browser. Preference test uses unconfigured provider admin access, allowing successful disable without any session-end assertion. Both tests miss a logout no-op.
evidence: MfaResetIntegrationTest.java:109–127 retains only an access token then calls fresh-browser MfaBrowser.login; MfaBrowser.java:104 creates a new OidcBrowser. MfaPolicyIntegrationTest.java:158–179 never exercises refresh/SSO invalidation; MfaController.java:120–129 permits missing/failed admin logout. Static coverage finding; no runtime logout failure claimed.
suggested_fix: Capture an existing refresh token and browser SSO session before reset and disable; assert refresh rejection and old-session loss afterward. Include provider failure behavior and web application sessions.
repro_test: Against CI containers, retain target browser and refresh token, reset or disable, then retry refresh and cookie-only authorization; a no-op logout mutation must fail the test.
